Among these, abrupt switching is particularly relevant for memristive operation and reverse-bias breakdown in solar cells. Summary / Abstract:
Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) hold strong potential for efficient and cost-effective photovoltaic technology, yet their device performance and stability remain hindered by interfacial limitations. In particular, the hole transport material (HTM) that contacts both the perovskite and the front contact can often be a bottleneck for device efficiency and durability. To overcome these challenges, we design and synthesize a series of carbazole- and fluorene-based polymers via palladium-catalyzed...

Summary / Abstract:
Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) are widely used as hole-selective contacts in inverted wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, incomplete SAM coverage and non-uniform interfacial contact of the SAMs/absorber induce recombination losses and interfacial degradation. Herein, we introduce carbohydrazide (CBH) as an interfacial modifier by interleaving it with SAMs to remedy their uncovered and weakly contacted interfacial regions. The CBH treatment improves interfacial uniformity...

This Review discusses cost-driven pathways towards industrially manufacturable perovskite photovoltaics, including improving manufacturing yield, reducing material costs and simplifying fabrication, as well as the remaining challenges for their industrial implementation.

item.title: Electronic structure of a persistent excitonic fluid far beyond the Mott limit
item.description:
Authors: Weiyan Qi, Stefano Ponzoni, Ashim Pramanik, Vitaly Gorelov, Yannis Laplace, Gianluca Stefanucci, Enrico Perfetto, Esteban Morcos, Marino Marsi, Steven Francis Udaundo, Sebastian Maherlein, Amina Taleb-Ibrahimi, Kaibo Zheng, Tonu Pullerits, Luca Perfetti
Journal: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org
Original feed: https://arxiv.org/rss/cond-mat
Published: 2026-10-26
Categories: cond-mat.other
id: oai:arXiv.org:2610.32437v1
guid: oai:arXiv.org:2610.32437v1
link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32437
published: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 00:00:00 -0400
updated: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 00:00:00 -0400
author: Weiyan Qi, Stefano Ponzoni, Ashim Pramanik, Vitaly Gorelov, Yannis Laplace, Gianluca Stefanucci, Enrico Perfetto, Esteban Morcos, Marino Marsi, Steven Francis Udaundo, Sebastian Maherlein, Amina Taleb-Ibrahimi, Kaibo Zheng, Tonu Pullerits, Luca Perfetti
rights: http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

Summary / Abstract:
arXiv:2610.32437v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Excitons are conventionally expected to destabilize at high photoexcitation densities, as screening weakens the electron-hole attraction. Recent studies, however, challenge this paradigm, suggesting that excitons generated by strong optical pumping can remain stable even beyond the onset of population inversion. Here, using time- and angle-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy on 2D hybrid perovskites, we provide direct evidence for such a high-density excitonic state, characterized by a distinctive Mexican-hat dispersion. Remarkably, this excitonic band reconstruction endures for orders of magnitude longer than the optical coherence time, revealing a population-sustained electronic structure that survives well into the incoherent regime. The excitonic resonance also persists far beyond optical saturation, at densities where exciton wavefunctions strongly overlap. Our findings reveal a long-lived, high-density quantum fluid of excitons with characteristics reminiscent of a BCS condensate, an electronic structure markedly different from that of the dilute limit.

item.title: Unifying Low-Frequency Raman and Infrared Signatures across Perovskites
item.description:
Authors: Ethan Berger, Erik Fransson, Apinya Ngoipala, Lucas Svensson, Priyanka Deswal, Mehmet Baskurt, Paul Erhart, Julia Wiktor
Journal: cond-mat updates on arXiv.org
Original feed: https://arxiv.org/rss/cond-mat
Published: 2026-10-26
Categories: cond-mat.mtrl-sci
id: oai:arXiv.org:2610.31830v1
guid: oai:arXiv.org:2610.31830v1
link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31830
published: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 00:00:00 -0400
updated: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 00:00:00 -0400
author: Ethan Berger, Erik Fransson, Apinya Ngoipala, Lucas Svensson, Priyanka Deswal, Mehmet Baskurt, Paul Erhart, Julia Wiktor
rights: http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

Summary / Abstract:
arXiv:2610.31830v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Perovskites have been studied for a wide range of applications, from oxide-based ferroelectrics to halide-perovskite photovoltaics. Despite their diverse functionalities, these materials share strong lattice anharmonicity arising from structural instabilities such as polar off-centering and octahedral tilting. These anharmonic distortions strongly influence the low-frequency vibrational response and can be observed in infrared (IR) and Raman spectra. However, low-frequency IR and Raman signatures are typically investigated separately, hindering the development of a unified understanding of vibrational spectroscopy across perovskite classes. In this work, we use machine-learning-based molecular dynamics to simulate the IR and Raman spectra of oxide perovskites (SrTiO$_3$ and BaTiO$_3$), halide perovskites (CsPbBr$_3$, CsSnBr$_3$, and CsGeBr$_3$) and double halide perovskites (Cs$_2$AgAlBr$_6$ and Cs$_2$AgBiBr$_6$). By comparing materials exhibiting polar, tilt-driven and mixed instabilities, we find that polar off-centering leads to enhanced low-frequency IR and dielectric responses, whereas nonpolar modes, particularly octahedral tilting, are associated with Raman central peaks. The strength of the low-frequency features also depends on how strongly the underlying modes couple to polarization or dielectric susceptibility. Finally, we show that the dynamics of these instabilities play an important role, with slow polar reorientations shifting the dielectric response to very low frequencies and overdamped tilting modes producing persistent Raman central peaks. These results establish a unified framework connecting low-frequency IR and Raman spectra to the symmetry, coupling and dynamics of their underlying anharmonic lattice instabilities.

item.title: Cross-coupled photon avalanche drives room-temperature intrinsic optical bistability
item.description:
Authors: Eva Conour, Jacob Wojcik, Jory Sanders, Abigale Puccini, Trey Stephens-Cherry, Artiom Skripka
Journal: physics updates on arXiv.org
Original feed: https://arxiv.org/rss/physics
Published: 2026-10-26
Categories: physics.optics; cond-mat.mtrl-sci
id: oai:arXiv.org:2610.32032v1
guid: oai:arXiv.org:2610.32032v1
link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32032
published: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 00:00:00 -0400
updated: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 00:00:00 -0400
author: Eva Conour, Jacob Wojcik, Jory Sanders, Abigale Puccini, Trey Stephens-Cherry, Artiom Skripka
rights: http://arxiv.org/licenses/nonexclusive-distrib/1.0/

Summary / Abstract:
arXiv:2610.32032v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optically bistable materials promise technological advances in optical information processing, memristive devices, and multiparametric sensing. However, optical bistability is predominantly observed under cryogenic conditions or is governed by subtle thermo-optical nonlinearities. Here, we report on Ho3+-activated nanocrystals that exhibit cavity-free intrinsic optical bistability (IOB) at ambient conditions. Non-thermal IOB stems from a cross-coupled photon avalanche (XPA) mechanism enabled by a low-phonon-energy double-perovskite host, which reduces nonradiative losses and facilitates excited-state population via XPA, even when the pump intensity is below threshold. Time-resolved luminescence measurements support the proposed XPA, as evidenced by a double-rise profile consistent with two reservoir states interlocked in energy looping. IOB with high-contrast photoswitching (up to 46 dB) is observed at room temperature across multiple visible emission lines, enabling wavelength-division multiplexing and compatibility with common detectors. IOB is preserved across nano- to microscale crystals and different double-perovskite compositions, broadly enabling information photonics and advanced sensing.
